image.zh: 《象》曰：上火下澤，睽。君子以同而異。
image.en: The Image states: Fire above, marsh below — Kui (Opposition). The noble person thereby shares in what is common yet preserves what is distinct.

1.zh: 初九，悔亡。喪馬，勿逐自復。見惡人，无咎。
1.en: Initial Nine: Regret vanishes. Losing a horse — do not pursue it; it will return of itself. If one sees an evil person, there is no blame.

wangBi.zh: 處睽之初，居下體之下，无應獨立，悔也。與四合志，故得悔亡。馬者，必顯之物。處物之始，乖而喪其馬，物莫能同其私，必相顯也，故勿逐而自復也。時方乖離，而位乎窮下，上无應可援，下无權可恃，顯德自異，為惡所害，故見惡人乃得免咎也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the beginning of Kui, dwelling at the bottom of the lower trigram, without a responsive counterpart and standing alone — this is cause for regret. Yet it shares its will with the fourth line, and therefore regret vanishes. A horse is a thing that necessarily stands out. At the beginning of things, amid divergence one loses one's horse, but nothing can conceal it in private — it will inevitably be made visible, so do not pursue it and it will return of itself. The time is one of divergence and separation; one's position is at the very bottom, with no responsive counterpart above to give aid and no power below to rely upon. To make one's virtue conspicuous and set oneself apart would invite harm from the wicked. Therefore, by meeting with the evil person, one is able to avoid blame.

2.zh: 九二，遇主于巷，无咎。
2.en: Nine in the Second: One meets the master in an alleyway. No blame.

wangBi.zh: 處睽失位，將无所安。然五亦失位，俱求其黨，出門同趣，不期而遇，故曰遇主於巷也。處睽得援，雖失其位，未失道也。
wangBi.en: Occupying a position in Kui while out of one's proper place, one is about to have nowhere to find rest. Yet the fifth line has also lost its proper place; both seek their kindred, going out and heading the same way, meeting unexpectedly — hence it says 'meets the master in an alleyway.' In the time of Kui one has found an ally; although one has lost one's position, one has not lost the Way.

3.zh: 六三，見輿曳，其牛掣。其人天且劓，无初有終。
3.en: Six in the Third: One sees the carriage dragged back, its ox restrained. The person is branded on the forehead and has the nose cut off. No beginning, but there is an end.

wangBi.zh: 凡物近而不相得則凶。處睽之時，履非其位，以陰居陽，以柔乘剛，志在於上，而不和於四。二應於五，則近而不相比，故見輿曳。輿曳者，履非其位，失所載也。其牛掣者，滯隔所在，不獲進也。「其人天且劓」者，四從上取，二從下取，而應在上九，執志不回。初雖受困，終獲剛助。
wangBi.en: In general, when things are near yet do not get along, there is misfortune. In the time of Kui, this line treads in a position that is not its own — yin occupying a yang place, the yielding riding atop the firm. Its will is set on what is above, yet it does not harmonize with the fourth line. The second responds to the fifth, so though near, they do not bond. Hence one sees the carriage dragged back. The carriage being dragged back means treading in the wrong position and losing what one carries. The ox being restrained means being stuck and blocked where one is, unable to advance. 'The person is branded on the forehead and has the nose cut off' — the fourth line attacks from above, the second attacks from below. Yet this line's responsive counterpart is Top Nine, and it holds fast to its will without turning back. Though at first it suffers hardship, in the end it obtains the aid of the firm.

4.zh: 九四，睽孤，遇元夫。交孚，厲，无咎。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth: Opposed and isolated, one meets a man of original character. Mutual trust through exchange. Danger, but no blame.

wangBi.zh: 无應獨處，五自應二，三與己睽，故曰睽孤也。初亦无應特立。處睽之時，俱在獨立，同處體下，同志者也。而己失位，比於三五，皆與己乖，處无所安，故求其疇類而自託焉，故曰遇元夫也。同志相得而无疑焉，故曰交孚也。雖在乖隔，志故得行，故雖危无咎。
wangBi.en: Without a responsive counterpart, dwelling alone — the fifth responds on its own to the second, and the third is in opposition with this line. Hence it says 'opposed and isolated.' The first line likewise has no responsive counterpart and stands alone. In the time of Kui, both stand in isolation; both occupy the lower part of their respective trigrams and share the same will. Yet this line has lost its position; the lines adjacent to it — the third and fifth — are all in discord with it; it has no place to find rest, and so it seeks out its kindred and entrusts itself to them. Hence it says 'meets a man of original character.' Sharing the same will, they find each other without doubt; hence 'mutual trust through exchange.' Although amid divergence and separation, their wills succeed in being carried out; therefore despite danger there is no blame.

5.zh: 六五，悔亡。厥宗噬膚，往，何咎？
5.en: Six in the Fifth: Regret vanishes. Its kinsman bites through the skin. Going forward — what blame could there be?

wangBi.zh: 非位，悔也。有應，故亡。厥宗，謂二也。噬膚者，齧柔也。三雖比二，二之所噬，非妨己應者也。以斯而往，何咎之有？往必合也。
wangBi.en: Not in its proper position — hence regret. Having a responsive counterpart — hence it vanishes. 'Its kinsman' refers to the second line. 'Biting through the skin' means gnawing through what is yielding. Although the third line is adjacent to the second, what the second bites through does not obstruct this line's responsive bond. Going forward under these conditions, what blame could there be? Going forward will certainly bring union.

6.zh: 上九，睽孤。見豕負塗，載鬼一車，先張之弧，後說之弧。匪寇婚媾，往，遇雨則吉。
6.en: Top Nine: Opposed and isolated. One sees a pig covered in mud, a cartload of ghosts. First one draws the bow, afterward one puts the bow aside. It is not a bandit but a marriage partner. Going forward, encountering rain brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 處睽之極，睽道未通，故曰睽孤。己居炎極，三處澤盛，睽之極也。以文明之極，而觀至穢之物，睽之甚也。豕而負塗，穢莫過焉。至睽將合，至殊將通，恢詭譎怪，道將為一。未至於洽，先見殊怪，故見豕負塗，甚可穢也。見鬼盈車，吁可怪也。先張之弧，將攻害也。後說之弧，睽怪通也。四剠其應，故為寇也。睽志將通，匪寇婚媾，往不失時，睽疑亡也。貴於遇雨，和陰陽也。陰陽既和，群疑亡也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the extreme of Kui, the way of opposition has not yet opened — hence 'opposed and isolated.' This line dwells at the extreme of flame, while the third line occupies the fullness of the marsh — this is the extreme of opposition. Viewing the most defiled of things from the extreme of civilized brightness — this is the utmost of opposition. A pig covered in mud — nothing could be filthier. When opposition reaches its extreme, union is about to come; when difference reaches its extreme, communication is about to open. The vast, the uncanny, the strange, and the monstrous — the Way is about to unify them all. Before harmony is reached, one first sees strange monstrosities; hence seeing a pig covered in mud, something supremely foul. Seeing ghosts filling a cart — how utterly bizarre! First drawing the bow — about to attack. Afterward putting the bow aside — the strangeness of opposition gives way to communication. The fourth line brands this line's responsive counterpart, and so appears as a bandit. But the will toward opposition is about to open into communication — it is not a bandit but a marriage partner. Going forward without missing the moment, the doubts of opposition vanish. The value of encountering rain lies in the harmonizing of yin and yang. Once yin and yang are harmonized, all doubts vanish.

image.zh:
《象》曰：山上有水，蹇。

君子以反身脩德。
image.en:
The Image says: Above the mountain there is water—Jian.

The noble person thereby turns inward to cultivate virtue.

1.en: Initial Six: Going forth meets obstruction; turning back brings praise.

wangBi.zh: 處難之始，居止之初，獨見前識，覩險而止，以待其時，知矣哉！故往則遇蹇，來則得譽。
wangBi.en: Situated at the beginning of difficulty, dwelling at the start of stopping, one alone perceives what lies ahead, sees danger and stops, waiting for the right time—how wise indeed! Therefore going forth encounters obstruction, while turning back gains praise.

2.zh: 六二，王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故。
2.en: Six in the Second: The king's minister struggles through obstruction upon obstruction—not for his own sake.

wangBi.zh: 處難之時*，履當其位，居不失中，以應於五。不以五在難中，私身遠害，執心不回，志匡王室者也。故曰：「王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故」。履中行義，以存其上，處蹇以此，未見其尤也。
wangBi.en: In a time of dwelling in difficulty*, one treads in the proper position, dwells without losing the center, and responds to the fifth line. One does not, because the fifth is amid difficulty, act selfishly to keep oneself distant from harm. Holding fast with unwavering heart, one's resolve is to assist the royal house. Therefore it says: 'The king's minister struggles through obstruction upon obstruction—not for his own sake.' Treading the center and practicing righteous meaning, thereby sustaining one's superior—handling Jian in this way, no fault is to be seen.

3.zh: 九三，往蹇，來反。
3.en: Nine in the Third: Going forth meets obstruction; turning back, one returns.

wangBi.zh: 進則入險，來則得位，故曰往蹇來反。為下卦之主，是內之所恃也。
wangBi.en: Advancing, one enters danger; turning back, one attains one's position. Therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction; turning back, one returns.' As the master of the lower trigram, this is what the inner [trigram] relies upon.

4.zh: 六四，往蹇，來連。
4.en: Six in the Fourth: Going forth meets obstruction; turning back, one joins [with others].

wangBi.zh: 往則无應，來則乘剛，往來皆難，故曰往蹇來連。得位履正，當其本實，雖遇於難，非妄所招也。
wangBi.en: Going forth, there is no corresponding line; turning back, one rides upon the strong. Going and coming are both difficult; therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction, turning back one joins.' Attaining one's position and treading correctly, fulfilling one's fundamental substance—though encountering difficulty, it is not something recklessly brought upon oneself.

5.zh: 九五，大蹇，朋來。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth: Great obstruction; companions come.

wangBi.zh: 處難之時，獨在險中，難之大者也，故曰大蹇。然居不失正，履不失中，執德之長，不改其節，如此則同志者集而至矣，故曰朋來也。
wangBi.en: In a time of dwelling in difficulty, alone amid danger—this is the greatest of difficulties; therefore it says 'great obstruction.' Yet dwelling without losing correctness, treading without losing the center, holding fast to virtue's constancy, and not changing one's integrity—being thus, those of like mind gather and arrive; therefore it says 'companions come.'

6.zh:
《象》曰：往蹇來碩，志在內也。

利見大人，以從貴也。
6.en:
The Image says: Going forth meets obstruction; turning back brings greatness—the resolve is directed inward.

Benefit in seeing a great person—thereby following the noble.

wangBi.zh:
往則長難，來則難終，難終則眾難皆濟，志大得矣，故曰往蹇來碩吉。險夷難解，大道可興，故曰利見大人也。

有應在內，往則失之*。來則志獲，志在內也。
wangBi.en:
Going forth prolongs difficulty; turning back brings difficulty to its end. When difficulty ends, all obstructions are overcome, and one's resolve is greatly fulfilled; therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction; turning back brings greatness—good fortune.' When danger is leveled and difficulty resolved, the great Way can flourish; therefore it says 'benefit in seeing a great person.'

There is a corresponding line within; going forth, one loses it*. Turning back, one's resolve is fulfilled—the resolve is directed inward.

readouts.name: Deliverance
readouts.question:
What can you
forgive?
readouts.lesson:
Out of danger?
Then don't linger.
readouts.finding: THUNDER BREAKS OUT OF THE WATER.

image.zh: 《象》曰：雷雨作，解，君子以赦過宥罪。
image.en: The Image says: Thunder and rain arise—Release. The noble person thereby pardons transgressions and shows leniency toward offenses.

1.en: Initial Six: No blame.

wangBi.zh:
解者，解也。屯難盤結，於是乎解也。處蹇難始解之初，在剛柔始散之際，將赦罪厄，以夷其險。處此之時，不煩於位而无咎也。

或有過咎，非其理也。義猶理也。
wangBi.en:
Release means untying. What was obstructed in difficulty and tangled together is here released. Situated at the very beginning when hardship and difficulty first begin to dissolve, at the juncture when the firm and the yielding first begin to disperse, offenses and distress are about to be pardoned, thereby leveling the danger. At such a time, one need not be troubled about one's position and is without blame.

If there were any error or blame, it would be contrary to principle. 'Meaning' here is equivalent to 'principle.'

2.zh: 九二，田獲三狐，得黃矢，貞吉。
2.en: Nine in the Second: In the hunt, three foxes are caught; a yellow arrow is obtained. Correctness brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 狐者，隱伏之物也。剛中而應，為五所任，處於險中，知險之情，以斯解物，能獲隱伏也，故曰「田獲三狐」也。黃，理中之稱也。矢，直也。田而獲三狐，得乎理中之道，不失枉直之實，能全其正者也，故曰「田獲三狐，得黃矢，貞吉」也。
wangBi.en: The fox is a creature that hides and lurks. Being firm and central with a corresponding line, it is entrusted by the Fifth. Situated within the danger, it knows the conditions of danger. Resolving things by this means, it can catch what is hidden and lurking; therefore it says 'in the hunt, three foxes are caught.' Yellow is a designation for the center of principle. Arrow (shi) means straight. Hunting and catching three foxes, one attains the Way of centered principle and does not lose the reality of what is crooked and what is straight, thereby fully preserving one's correctness. Therefore it says 'in the hunt, three foxes are caught; a yellow arrow is obtained; correctness brings good fortune.'

3.zh: 六三，負且乘，致寇至，貞吝。
3.en: Six in the Third: Carrying a burden while riding in a carriage, one invites bandits to come. Correctness brings regret.

wangBi.zh: 處非其位，履非其正，以附於四，用夫柔邪以自媚者也。乘二負四，以容其身。寇之來也，自己所致，雖幸而免，正之所賤也。
wangBi.en: Occupying a position that is not its own, treading where it has no rightful place, it attaches itself to the Fourth, using yielding flattery to ingratiate itself. It rides upon the Second and bears the burden of the Fourth, thereby finding accommodation for itself. The coming of bandits is brought about by oneself. Even if one is fortunate enough to escape, it is something that correctness despises.

4.zh: 九四，解而拇，朋至斯孚。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth: Release your big toe; then allies will come with trust.

wangBi.zh: 失位不正，而比於三，故三得附之為其拇也。三為之拇，則失初之應，故解其拇，然後朋至而信矣。
wangBi.en: Having lost its proper position and being incorrect, it is adjacent to the Third; therefore the Third is able to attach to it as its big toe. If the Third serves as its big toe, then the correspondence with the Initial line is lost. Therefore one must release the big toe, and only then will allies come with trust.

5.zh: 六五，君子維有解，吉。有孚于小人。
5.en: Six in the Fifth: The noble person herein achieves release—good fortune. There is trust shown toward the petty person.

wangBi.zh: 居尊履中而應乎剛，可以有解而獲吉矣。以君子之道解難釋險，小人雖闇，猶知服之而无怨矣。故曰「有孚于小人」也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the honored position, treading in the center, and corresponding with the firm, it can achieve release and obtain good fortune. When one uses the Way of the noble person to release difficulty and dissolve danger, even though the petty person is benighted, he still knows to submit and bears no resentment. Therefore it says 'there is trust shown toward the petty person.'

6.zh: 上六，公用射隼于高墉之上，獲之，无不利。
6.en: Top Six: The duke shoots a hawk upon the high wall. He catches it. Nothing is unfavorable.

wangBi.zh: 初為四應，二為五應，三不應上，失位負乘，處下體之上，故曰高墉。墉非隼之所處，高非三之所履，上六居動之上，為解之極，將解荒悖而除穢亂者也。故用射之，極而後動，成而後舉，故必獲之而无不利也。
wangBi.en: The Initial line corresponds with the Fourth; the Second corresponds with the Fifth. The Third does not correspond with Top Six. It has lost its position and carries a burden while riding, and it occupies the top of the lower trigram; therefore it is called the 'high wall.' A wall is not a place where a hawk should perch; a height is not where the Third should tread. Top Six dwells at the top of the movement trigram and is the culmination of Release. It is about to release what is dissolute and perverse and to eliminate what is foul and disordered. Therefore it uses shooting. Acting only at the culmination, moving only after conditions are ripe, proceeding only after success is assured—therefore it necessarily catches it, and nothing is unfavorable.

image.zh:
《象》曰：山下有澤，損。

君子以懲忿窒欲。
image.en:
The Image states: Below the mountain there is a lake — Decrease.

The noble person uses this to curb anger and restrain desires.

1.zh: 初九，已事遄往，无咎，酌損之。
1.en: Initial Nine: When the task is finished, go swiftly. No blame. Consider carefully how to decrease.

wangBi.zh:
損之為道，損下益上，損剛益柔，以應其時者也。居於下極，損剛奉柔，則不可以逸。處損之始，則不可以盈。時已則往，不敢宴安，乃獲无咎也。剛以奉柔，雖免乎咎，猶未親也，故既獲无咎，復自酌損，乃得合志也。遄，速也。

尚合於志，故速往也。
wangBi.en:
The Way of Decrease is to decrease the lower to benefit the upper, to decrease the firm to benefit the yielding, in response to the demands of the time. Occupying the lowest position and decreasing firmness to serve yielding, one must not be idle. Being at the beginning of Decrease, one must not be complacent. When the task is already done, then go — not daring to rest at ease — and only then will one obtain no blame. Using firmness to serve yielding, although one avoids blame, there is not yet closeness. Therefore, having obtained no blame, one further carefully measures how to decrease oneself, and only then achieves alignment of wills. "Chuan" (遄) means "swiftly."

One hopes to align wills, and therefore goes swiftly.

2.zh: 九二，利貞，征凶。弗損，益之。
2.en: Nine in the Second: Benefit in Correctness. To advance brings misfortune. Do not decrease; increase it instead.

wangBi.zh: 柔不可全益，剛不可全削，下不可以无正。初九已損剛以順柔，九二履中，而復損己以益柔，則剝道成焉，故不可遄往，而利貞也。進之於柔，則凶矣，故曰征凶也。故九二不損而務益，以中為志也。
wangBi.en: Yielding cannot be entirely increased, nor can firmness be entirely stripped away; the lower cannot be without Correctness. Initial Nine has already decreased firmness to comply with yielding. If Nine in the Second, treading the central position, were again to diminish itself to benefit yielding, then the Way of Stripping (Bo, hexagram 23) would be realized. Therefore one must not go swiftly but rather find Benefit in Correctness. To advance toward yielding would be misfortune; hence it says "to advance brings misfortune." Therefore Nine in the Second does not decrease itself but devotes effort to increase, taking the center as its guiding purpose.

3.zh: 六三，三人行則損一人，一人行則得其友。
3.en: Six in the Third: When three people travel together, one person is decreased. When one person travels alone, one finds a companion.

wangBi.zh: 損之為道，損下益上，其道上行。三人，謂自六三已上三陰也。三陰並行，以承於上，則上失其友，內无其主，名之曰益，其實乃損。故天地相應，乃得化淳；男女匹配，乃得化生。陰陽不對，生可得乎？故六三獨行，乃得其友，三陰俱行，則必疑矣。
wangBi.en: The Way of Decrease is to decrease the lower to benefit the upper; its Way moves upward. "Three people" refers to the three yin lines from Six in the Third upward. If the three yin lines travel together to serve the one above, then the upper loses its companion, and within there is no master — this is called Increase in name, but in reality it is Decrease. Thus when heaven and earth correspond with each other, transformation achieves purity; when man and woman are properly matched, procreation is achieved. If yin and yang are not properly paired, can life be attained? Therefore, when Six in the Third travels alone, it finds its companion. If all three yin lines travel together, then there will surely be suspicion.

4.zh: 六四，損其疾，使遄有喜，无咎。
4.en: Six in the Fourth: Decrease one's affliction. Act swiftly and there will be joy. No blame.

wangBi.zh: 履得其位，以柔納剛，能損其疾也。疾何可久，故速乃有喜。損疾以離其咎，有喜乃免，故使速乃有喜，有喜乃无咎也。
wangBi.en: Treading in its proper position and receiving firmness through yielding, it can decrease its affliction. An affliction cannot be endured for long; therefore acting swiftly brings joy. Decreasing the affliction in order to depart from blame — only with joy is one absolved. Therefore acting swiftly brings joy, and with joy there is no blame.

5.zh: 六五，或益之，十朋之龜弗克違，元吉。
5.en: Six in the Fifth: Someone increases it. A tortoise worth ten sets of cowries cannot gainsay this. Sublime Beginning good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 以柔居尊，而為損道，江海處下，百谷歸之。履尊以損，則或益之矣。朋，黨也。龜者，決疑之物也。陰非先唱，柔非自任，尊以自居，損以守之。故人用其力，事竭其功，知者慮能，明者慮策，弗能違也，則眾才之用盡矣。獲益而得十朋之龜，足以盡天人之助也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the honored position with yielding and practicing the Way of Decrease — like rivers and seas that dwell in the lowest place, and all the valleys flow toward them. Treading the position of honor with Decrease, then someone will increase it. "Peng" (朋) means "associates" or "groups." The tortoise is an instrument for resolving doubt. Yin does not initiate; yielding does not take charge on its own. Dwelling in the honored position and maintaining it through Decrease — therefore people devote their strength, affairs exhaust their merit, the wise deliberate with their abilities, and the perceptive deliberate with their strategies, unable to gainsay it. Then the full use of all talents is exhausted. To receive increase and obtain a tortoise worth ten sets of cowries is sufficient to exhaust the aid of both heaven and humans.

6.zh: 上九，弗損，益之，无咎，貞吉。利有攸往，得臣无家。
6.en: Top Nine: Not decreased, but increased. No blame. Correctness brings good fortune. It is Beneficial to have somewhere to go. One gains ministers but has no private household.

wangBi.zh: 處損之終，上无所奉，損終反益，剛德不損，乃反益之，而不憂於咎。用正而吉，不制於柔，剛德遂長，故曰｢弗損，益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往｣也。居上乘柔，處損之極，尚夫剛德，為物所歸，故曰得臣。得臣則天下為一，故无家也。
wangBi.en: Situated at the end of Decrease, above there is no one to serve. At the end of Decrease it reverses into Increase; the virtue of firmness is not diminished but rather increased, and there is no worry of blame. Employing Correctness brings good fortune. Not controlled by yielding, the virtue of firmness continues to grow. Hence it says, "Not decreased, but increased; no blame; Correctness brings good fortune; it is Beneficial to have somewhere to go." Dwelling above and riding upon yielding, situated at the extreme of Decrease, valuing the virtue of firmness — all beings return to it. Hence it says, "gains ministers." When one gains ministers, then all under heaven becomes one; hence "no private household."

readouts.name: Gathering Together
readouts.question:
What holds your
group together?
readouts.lesson:
Gather people by
what is right.
readouts.finding: FOUR YIELDING LINES GATHER TO TWO.

image.zh: 《象》曰：澤上於地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。
image.en: The Image states: The lake rises above the earth—Gathering. The noble person thereby readies weapons of war and guards against the unforeseen.

1.zh: 初六，有孚不終，乃亂乃萃。若號一握為笑，勿恤，往无咎。
1.en: Initial Six: There is sincerity that does not last to the end; then there is disorder, then gathering. If one calls out, a single handful becomes laughter. Do not worry—going forward is without blame.

wangBi.zh: 有應在四而三承之，心懷嫌疑，故有孚不終也。不能守道，以結至好，迷務競爭，故乃亂乃萃也。一握者，小之貌也。為笑者，懦劣之貌也。己為正配，三以近寵，若安夫卑退，謙以自牧，則勿恤而往无咎也。
wangBi.en: There is a correspondence with the fourth, yet the third encroaches upon it. The heart harbors suspicion and doubt, hence "there is sincerity that does not last to the end." Unable to hold to the Way and form the most excellent bond, confused and occupied with contention, hence "then there is disorder, then gathering." "A single handful" is an image of smallness. "Becoming laughter" is an image of timidity and weakness. Oneself is the proper match, yet the third gains favor through proximity. If one is content with humility and withdrawal, using modesty to govern oneself, then there will be no worry and going forward is without blame.

2.zh: 六二，引吉无咎，孚乃利用禴。
2.en: Six in the Second: Being drawn forward brings good fortune and is without blame. With sincerity, it is then Beneficial to use the Yue sacrifice.

wangBi.zh: 居萃之時，體柔當位，處坤之中，己獨處正，與眾相殊，異操而聚，民之多僻，獨正者危。未能變體以遠於害，故必見引，然後乃吉而无咎也。禴，殷春祭名也，四時祭之省者也。居聚之時，處於中正，而行以忠信，故可以省薄薦於鬼神也。
wangBi.en: At the time of Gathering, having a yielding nature in the proper position, dwelling in the center of Kun, one alone occupies the correct position, differing from the multitude. Gathering with different conduct—when the people are mostly deviant, the one who alone is correct is in danger. Unable to change one's nature to distance oneself from harm, one must necessarily be drawn forward, and only then is there good fortune and no blame. The "Yue" is the name of the Yin dynasty's spring sacrifice, the simplest of the four seasonal sacrifices. At the time of gathering, dwelling in centrality and correctness, and acting with loyalty and sincerity, one may use simple and modest offerings to present to the ghosts and spirits.

3.zh: 六三，萃如，嗟如，无攸利。往无咎，小吝。
3.en: Six in the Third: Gathering thus, sighing thus—nothing is Beneficial. Going forward is without blame, but there is slight regret.

wangBi.zh: 履非其位，以比於四，四亦失位。不正相聚，相聚不正，患所生也。干人之應，害所起也，故「萃如嗟如，无攸利」也。上六亦无應而獨立，處極而憂危，思援而求朋，巽以待物者也。與其萃於不正，不若之於同志，故可以往而无咎也。二陰相合，猶不若一陰一陽之應*，故有小吝也。
wangBi.en: Treading in an improper position and being close to the fourth, yet the fourth also has lost its position. Gathering together improperly—when those who gather together are not correct, troubles arise. Intruding upon another's correspondence is where harm originates. Hence "gathering thus, sighing thus—nothing is Beneficial." Top Six also has no correspondence and stands alone, dwelling at the extreme and anxious about danger, seeking aid and looking for companions, humbly yielding in receiving others. Rather than gathering with what is not correct, it is better to go to one of the same aspiration. Hence one may go forward and be without blame. Yet two yin lines joining together is still not as good as a yin and yang correspondence*; hence there is slight regret.

4.zh: 九四，大吉，无咎。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth: Great good fortune, and no blame.

wangBi.zh: 履非其位而下據三陰，得其所據，失其所處。處聚之時，不正而據，故必大吉，立夫大功，然後无咎也。
wangBi.en: Treading in an improper position yet commanding the three yin lines below—obtaining what it commands but losing its proper place. At the time of Gathering, being incorrect yet commanding, therefore one must attain great good fortune and establish great merit, and only then will there be no blame.

5.zh: 九五，萃有位，无咎，匪孚。元永貞，悔亡。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth: Gathering while possessing the position—no blame. There is a lack of trust. With a Sublime Beginning, perpetual Correctness, regret vanishes.

wangBi.zh: 處聚之時，最得盛位，故曰萃有位也。四專而據，己德不行，自守而已，故曰无咎匪孚。夫脩仁守正，久必悔消，故曰「元永貞，悔亡」。
wangBi.en: At the time of Gathering, occupying the most exalted position, hence it says "gathering while possessing the position." The fourth monopolizes command, and one's own virtue cannot be carried out; one merely guards oneself. Hence it says "no blame; there is a lack of trust." If one cultivates benevolence and maintains correctness, in time regret will surely vanish. Hence it says "with a Sublime Beginning, perpetual Correctness, regret vanishes."

6.zh: 上六，齎咨涕洟，无咎。
6.en: Top Six: Lamenting and sighing, weeping and sniveling—no blame.

wangBi.zh: 處聚之時，居於上極，五非所乘，內无應援。處上獨立，近遠无助，危莫甚焉。齎咨，嗟歎之辭也。若能知危之至，懼禍之深，憂病之甚，至於涕洟，不敢自安，亦眾所不害，故得无咎也。
wangBi.en: At the time of Gathering, dwelling at the uppermost extreme, the fifth is not one to be ridden upon, and inwardly there is no corresponding support. Dwelling above and standing alone, near and far there is no aid—nothing is more perilous than this. "Lamenting and sighing" are words of sorrowful exclamation. If one can recognize that danger has arrived, fear the depth of calamity, and be anxious about affliction to the utmost, to the point of weeping and sniveling, not daring to rest at ease, then the multitude will also not harm one. Hence there is no blame.

readouts.question:

readouts.finding: WOOD UNDER EARTH, GROWING UP.

image.zh: 《象》曰：地中生木，升。君子以順德，積小以高大。
image.en: The Image says: Trees grow within the earth—this is Ascending. The noble person, in accordance with this, cultivates virtue through compliance and accumulates small things to achieve greatness.

1.en: Initial Six. Sincerely ascending—great good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 允，當也。巽卦三爻，皆升者也。雖无其應，處升之初，與九二、九三合志俱升。當升之時，升必大得，是以大吉也。
wangBi.en: Yun means 'fitting' or 'sincere.' The three lines of the Xun trigram are all ascending. Although this line has no correspondent, it occupies the beginning of Ascending and joins its intent with Nine in the Second and Nine in the Third, ascending together. At the time of ascending, the ascent necessarily brings great attainment—therefore there is great good fortune.

2.zh: 九二，孚乃利用禴，无咎。
2.en: Nine in the Second. If there is sincerity, then it is beneficial to perform the Yue sacrifice—no blame.

wangBi.zh: 與五為應，往必見任。體夫剛德，進不求寵，閑邪存誠，志在大業，故乃利用納約于神明矣。
wangBi.en: It corresponds with the Fifth, so going forth it will certainly be entrusted with responsibility. Embodying the virtue of firmness, it advances without seeking favor, guards against deviance and preserves sincerity, and its intent lies in great undertakings. Therefore it is beneficial to present modest offerings to the spirits.

3.zh: 九三，升虛邑。
3.en: Nine in the Third. Ascending into an empty city.

wangBi.zh:
履得其位，以陽升陰，以斯而舉，莫之違距，故若升虛邑也。

往必得也。
wangBi.en:
It treads in its proper position and ascends as yang toward yin. Rising in this manner, nothing opposes or resists it, so it is as if ascending into an empty city.

Going forth, one will certainly succeed.

4.zh: 六四，王用亨於岐山，吉，无咎。
4.en: Six in the Fourth. The king makes offerings at Mount Qi—good fortune, no blame.

wangBi.zh: 處升之際，下升而進，可納而不可距也。距下之進，攘來自專，則殃咎至焉。若能不距而納，順物之情，以通庶志，則得吉而无咎矣。岐山之會，順事之情，无不納也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the juncture of ascending, those below ascend and advance—they can be received but not resisted. To resist the advance of those below, seizing what comes and acting with self-serving exclusivity, would bring calamity and blame. If one can refrain from resisting and instead receive them, following the natural inclinations of things and opening a channel for the many intentions, then one attains good fortune and is without blame. At the gathering at Mount Qi, King Wen followed the natural course of affairs and received all without exception.

5.zh: 六五，貞吉，升階。
5.en: Six in the Fifth. Correctness brings good fortune—ascending the stairs.

wangBi.zh: 升得尊位，體柔而應，納而不距，任而不專，故得貞吉，升階而尊也。
wangBi.en: Ascending to attain the honored position, its nature is yielding and it has a correspondence. It receives and does not resist, delegates and does not monopolize. Therefore it attains correctness and good fortune, ascending the stairs to the honored place.

6.zh: 上六，冥升，利于不息之貞。
6.en: Top Six. Ascending in darkness—it is beneficial to maintain the correctness of ceaseless effort.

wangBi.zh:
處升之極，進而不息者也。進而不息，故雖冥猶升也。故施於不息之正則可，用於為物之主則喪矣。終於不息，消之道也。

勞不可久也。
wangBi.en:
Occupying the extreme of ascending, this is one who advances without ceasing. Advancing without ceasing, even in darkness one still ascends. Therefore, if applied to the correctness of ceaseless effort, it is acceptable; but if used to serve as the master of things, it leads to ruin. To persist in ceaselessness to the end is the way of diminishment.

Exertion cannot be sustained long.

readouts.name: Revolution
readouts.hook: Making a big change nobody believes in?
meaning:
Trust comes on
the last day.
readouts.question:
What change are
you making?
readouts.lesson:
For a revolution,
a new calendar.
readouts.finding: FIRE IN THE LAKE. ONE MUST GIVE.

image.zh: 《象》曰：澤中有火，革。君子以治歷明時。
image.en: The Image states: Within the lake there is fire — Revolution. The noble person thereby regulates the calendar and clarifies the seasons.

1.en: Initial Nine: Bound firmly with the hide of a yellow ox.

wangBi.zh: 在革之始，革道未成，固夫常中，未能應變者也。此可以守成，不可以有為也。鞏，固也。黃，中也。牛之革，堅仞不可變也。固之所用，常中堅仞，不肯變也。
wangBi.en: At the beginning of Revolution, the Way of revolution is not yet accomplished. One holds fast to the constant center, not yet able to respond to change. This is suitable for maintaining what has been accomplished, but not for taking action. "Bound firmly" (gong) means to secure firmly. "Yellow" represents the center. The hide of an ox is tough and unyielding, impossible to change. What is used to hold firm is the constant center, tough and unyielding, unwilling to change.

2.zh: 六二，已日乃革之，征吉，无咎。
2.en: Six in the Second: When the day is done, then carry out the revolution. Advancing brings good fortune, no blame.

wangBi.zh: 陰之為物，不能先唱，順從者也。不能自革，革已乃能從之，故曰「已日乃革之」也。二與五雖有水火殊體之異，同處厥中，陰陽相應，往必合志，不憂咎也，是以征吉而无咎。
wangBi.en: Yin by its nature cannot take the lead; it is a follower. It cannot initiate revolution on its own, but once revolution has been accomplished it can follow — hence it says "when the day is done, then carry out the revolution." Though the second and fifth lines have the difference of water and fire as separate trigram bodies, they both occupy their respective centers. Yin and yang correspond to each other; going forth they must unite in purpose and need not worry about blame. Therefore advancing brings good fortune and there is no blame.

3.zh: 九三，征凶，貞厲。革言三就，有孚。
3.en: Nine in the Third: Advancing brings misfortune. Correctness brings danger. When the call for revolution is thrice affirmed, there is trust.

wangBi.zh: 已處火極，上卦三爻，雖體水性，皆從革者也。自四至上，從命而變，不敢有違，故曰革言三就。其言實誠，故曰有孚。革言三就，有孚而猶征之，凶其宜也。
wangBi.en: Already situated at the extreme of fire, the three lines of the upper trigram, though their trigram body is of the nature of water, all follow the revolution. From the fourth to the top, they obey the mandate and transform, not daring to defy. Hence it says "the call for revolution is thrice affirmed." Their words are true and sincere, hence it says "there is trust." When the call for revolution is thrice affirmed and there is trust, yet one still advances — misfortune is fitting.

4.zh: 九四，悔亡，有孚，改命吉。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth: Regret vanishes. There is trust. Changing the mandate brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh:
初九處下卦之下，九四處上卦之下，故能變也。无應，悔也。與水火相比，能變者也，是以悔亡。處水火之際，居會變之始，能不固吝，不疑於下，信志改命，不失時願，是以吉也。有孚則見信矣，見信以改命，則物安而无違，故曰「悔亡，有孚，改命吉」也。處上體之下，始宣命也。

信志而行。
wangBi.en:
Initial Nine occupies the bottom of the lower trigram; Nine in the Fourth occupies the bottom of the upper trigram — therefore it can change. Having no corresponding line is cause for regret. But being adjacent to water and fire and capable of transformation — this is why regret vanishes. Situated at the juncture of water and fire, occupying the beginning of converging transformation, it can avoid obstinate stinginess and does not doubt those below. Trusting its purpose to change the mandate and not missing the aspirations of the time — this is why there is good fortune. When there is trust one is believed; being believed while changing the mandate, then all things are at ease and none defy — hence it says "regret vanishes, there is trust, changing the mandate brings good fortune." Occupying the bottom of the upper trigram body, one begins to proclaim the mandate.

Trusting one's purpose and proceeding.

5.zh: 九五，大人虎變，未占有孚。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth: The great person transforms like a tiger. Without divination there is trust.

wangBi.zh: 未占而孚，合時心也。
wangBi.en: Without divination there is trust — it accords with the hearts of the time.

6.zh:
上六，君子豹變，小人革面。

征凶，居貞吉。
6.en:
Top Six: The noble person transforms like a leopard; the petty person changes only their outward appearance.

Advancing brings misfortune. Remaining in correctness brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh:
居變之終，變道已成，君子處之，能成其文。小人樂成，則變面以順上也。

改命創制，變道已成，功成則事損，事損則无為。故居則得正而吉，征則躁擾而凶也。
wangBi.en:
Dwelling at the end of transformation, the Way of change is already accomplished. The noble person, situated here, can bring his cultural refinement to completion. The petty person rejoices in accomplishment and changes only his outward appearance to comply with those above.

The mandate has been changed and institutions created; the Way of transformation is already accomplished. When merit is achieved, then affairs are reduced; when affairs are reduced, there is non-action. Therefore remaining in place brings correctness and good fortune, while advancing brings agitation and disturbance and hence misfortune.

readouts.name: Keeping Still
meaning:
Stay with where
you are now.
readouts.question: What can wait?
readouts.lesson:
Stop when it's
time to stop.
readouts.finding: NO PAIR ANSWERS. EACH STANDS STILL.

image.zh: 《象》曰：兼山，艮，君子以思，不出其位。
image.en: The Image says: Mountains joined together form Gen. The noble person, accordingly, thinks without going beyond his position.

1.zh:
初六，艮其趾，无咎；利永貞。

象曰：艮其趾，未失正也。
1.en:
Initial Six: Keeping still at one's toes—no blame. Benefit in lasting Correctness.

The Image says: Keeping still at one's toes means one has not yet lost what is correct.

wangBi.zh: 處止之初，行无所之，故止其趾乃得无咎。至靜而定，故利永貞。
wangBi.en: Dwelling at the beginning of stopping, there is nowhere to go by moving; therefore stopping at the toes brings no blame. Being utterly still and settled, therefore there is Benefit in lasting Correctness.

2.zh:
六二，艮其腓，不拯其隨，其心不快。

象曰：不拯其隨，未退聽也。
2.en:
Six in the Second: Keeping still at one's calves. One cannot lift what follows along; one's heart is not glad.

The Image says: Not lifting what follows along—one has not yet withdrawn to listen obediently.

wangBi.zh: 隨，謂趾也。止其腓，故其趾不拯也。腓體躁而處止，而不得拯其隨，又不能退聽安靜，故其心不快也。
wangBi.en: "What follows" refers to the toes. Stopping the calves means the toes cannot be lifted. The calves are restless in nature yet are placed in stillness; unable to lift what follows, and also unable to withdraw and listen in quiet composure, therefore one's heart is not glad.

3.zh:
九三，艮其限，列其夤，厲薰心。

象曰：艮其限，危薰心也。
3.en:
Nine in the Third: Keeping still at one's waist. The flesh along the spine is split apart; danger sears the heart.

The Image says: Keeping still at one's waist—peril sears the heart.

wangBi.zh: 限，身之中也。三當兩象之中，故曰艮其限。夤，當中脊之肉也。止加其身，中體而分，故列其夤而憂危薰心也。艮之為義，各止於其所，上下不相與，至中則列矣。列加其夤，危莫甚焉，危亡之憂，乃薰灼其心也。施止體中，其體分焉，體分兩主，大器喪矣。
wangBi.en: "Waist" (xian) is the middle of the body. The third line falls at the juncture of the two trigram images; therefore it says "keeping still at the waist." "Yin" (yi) refers to the flesh along the middle of the spine. Stopping is imposed upon the body at its center, dividing the body; therefore the flesh of the spine is split apart and the worry of danger sears the heart. The meaning of Gen is that each stops in its proper place, with upper and lower not interacting; when one reaches the middle, there is splitting. When the splitting reaches the flesh of the spine, nothing is more perilous. The anxiety of danger and ruin thus sears and scorches the heart. When stopping is applied at the center of the body, the body is divided; when the body is divided into two ruling parts, the great vessel is lost.

4.zh:
六四，艮其身，无咎。

象曰：艮其身，止諸躬也。
4.en:
Six in the Fourth: Keeping still at one's whole body—no blame.

The Image says: Keeping still at one's whole body means stopping at one's own person.

wangBi.zh:
中上稱身，履得其位，止求諸身，得其所處，故不陷於咎也。

自止其躬，不分全體。
wangBi.en:
The middle and upper portions are called the body. Treading in one's proper position, one seeks to stop within one's own body and finds one's proper place; therefore one does not fall into blame.

One stops at one's own person without dividing the whole body.

5.zh:
六五，艮其輔，言有序，悔亡。

象曰：艮其輔，以中正也。
5.en:
Six in the Fifth: Keeping still at one's jaws. Words are well-ordered; regret vanishes.

The Image says: Keeping still at one's jaws—because of centrality and correctness.

wangBi.zh:
施止於輔，以處於中，故口无擇言，能亡其悔也。

能用中正，故言有序也。
wangBi.en:
Applying stopping to the jaws, and dwelling in the center, one's mouth has no ill-chosen words and is able to make regret vanish.

Being able to employ centrality and correctness, therefore words are well-ordered.

6.zh:
上九，敦艮，吉。

象曰：敦艮之吉，以厚終也。
6.en:
Top Nine: Magnanimous keeping still—auspicious.

The Image says: The auspiciousness of magnanimous keeping still is because of ending with generosity.

wangBi.zh: 居止之極，極止者也。敦重在上，不陷非妄，宜其吉也。
wangBi.en: Dwelling at the extreme of stopping, this is the utmost of stopping. Generous and weighty in the uppermost position, one does not fall into error or recklessness; it is fitting that there be auspiciousness.

readouts.name: Development
meaning:
Development says:
go step by step.
readouts.question:
Which step are
you skipping?
readouts.lesson:
Earn each place
before the next.
readouts.finding: LINES 2 TO 5 ALL IN THEIR PLACE.

image.zh: 《象》曰：山上有木，漸，君子以居賢德善俗。
image.en: The Image says: On the mountain there are trees — Gradual Advance. The noble person thereby establishes worthy virtue and improves customs.

1.zh: 初六，鴻漸于干，小子厲，有言，无咎。
1.en: Initial Six. The wild goose gradually advances to the riverbank. The young son is in danger. There are words of blame. No fault.

wangBi.zh: 鴻，水鳥也。適進之義，始於下而升者也，故以鴻為喻。六爻皆以進而履之為義焉，始進而位乎窮下，又无其應。若履于干，危不可以安也。始進而未得其位，則困於小子，窮於謗言，故曰小子厲有言也。困於小子讒諛之言，未傷君子之義，故曰无咎也。
wangBi.en: The hong is a water bird. In the meaning of proceeding to advance, it begins from below and ascends, hence the wild goose is used as a metaphor. All six lines take advancing and treading upon their position as their meaning. Beginning to advance yet positioned at the very bottom, with no corresponding line above — it is like treading upon the riverbank, dangerous and unable to find security. Beginning to advance but not yet having attained one's position, one is beset by petty persons and harassed by slanderous words, hence it says 'the young son is in danger, there are words of blame.' Being beset by the flattering and slanderous words of petty persons does not injure the meaning of the noble person, hence it says 'no fault.'

2.zh: 六二，鴻漸于磐，飲食衎衎，吉。
2.en: Six in the Second. The wild goose gradually advances to the large rock. Eating and drinking in contentment. Auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 磐，山石之安者也。進而得位，居中而應，本无祿養，進而得之，其為歡樂，願莫先焉。
wangBi.en: Pan is a stable mountain rock. Advancing and attaining one's position, dwelling in the center with a corresponding line — originally without salary or sustenance, but advancing and obtaining them. The resulting joy and happiness surpass all other wishes.

3.zh: 《象》曰：夫征不復，離群醜也。婦孕不育，失其道也。利用禦寇，順相保也。
3.en: The Image says: The husband goes on campaign and does not return — he separates from his group and kin. The wife is pregnant but does not give birth — she has lost the Way. It is beneficial to ward off enemies — they protect each other through compliance.

wangBi.zh: 陸，高之頂也。進而之陸，與四相得，不能復反者也。夫征不復，樂於邪配，則婦亦不能執貞矣。非夫而孕，故不育也。三本艮體，而棄乎群醜，與四相得，遂乃不反，至使婦孕不育，見利忘義，貪進忘舊，凶之道也。異體合好，順而相保，物莫能間，故利禦寇也。
wangBi.en: Lu is the top of the heights. Advancing to reach the plateau, it finds mutual affinity with the fourth line and cannot turn back. The husband goes on campaign and does not return, delighting in an improper union; the wife then also cannot maintain her fidelity. Pregnant by one who is not her husband, she therefore does not give birth. The third line originally belongs to the Gen trigram body, yet abandons its group and kin, finds mutual affinity with the fourth line, and consequently does not return. This leads to the wife being pregnant but not giving birth — seeing benefit and forgetting meaning, being greedy for advancement and forgetting old ties — this is the way of misfortune. When different trigram bodies form a bond, they protect each other through compliance, and nothing can come between them, hence it is beneficial to ward off enemies.

4.zh: 《象》曰：或得其桷，順以巽也。
4.en: The Image says: Perhaps finding a flat branch to perch on — through compliance and deference.

wangBi.zh: 鳥而之木，得其宜也。或得其桷，遇安棲也。雖乘于剛，志相得也。
wangBi.en: A bird going to a tree finds what is suitable for it. 'Perhaps finding a flat branch to perch on' means encountering a safe roosting place. Although it rides above the firm line, their intentions find mutual affinity.

5.zh: 九五，鴻漸于陵。婦三歲不孕，終莫之勝，吉。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth. The wild goose gradually advances to the hilltop. The wife does not conceive for three years. In the end, nothing can overcome this. Auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 陵，次陸者也。進得中位，而隔乎三四，不得與其應合，故婦三歲不孕也。各履正而居中，三四不能久塞其塗者也。不過三歲，必得所願矣。進以正邦，三年有成，成則道濟，故不過三歲也。
wangBi.en: Ling (hilltop) is next in elevation after the plateau. Advancing and attaining the central position, yet separated by the third and fourth lines, unable to unite with its corresponding line — hence the wife does not conceive for three years. Each treads upon what is correct and dwells in the center; the third and fourth lines cannot long obstruct their path. After no more than three years, one will surely obtain what one desires. Advancing to bring Correctness to the state, in three years there is accomplishment. Once accomplished, the Way is fulfilled, hence it does not exceed three years.

6.zh: 上九，鴻漸于陸。其羽可用為儀，吉。
6.en: Top Nine. The wild goose gradually advances to the high plateau. Its feathers can be used as ceremonial ornaments. Auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 進處高絜，不累於位，无物可以屈其心而亂其志。峨峨清遠，儀可貴也，故曰「其羽可用為儀，吉」。
wangBi.en: Advancing to dwell in a lofty and pure place, unburdened by official position, nothing can bend its heart or disorder its will. Towering, pure, and transcendent, its deportment is worthy of esteem. Hence it says 'its feathers can be used as ceremonial ornaments, auspicious.'

readouts.name: The Marrying Maiden
meaning:
Marrying Maiden
says: see the end.
readouts.question:
What does the
end look like?
readouts.lesson:
Wrong place?
Don't push.
readouts.finding: LINES 2 TO 5 ALL OUT OF PLACE.

image.zh: 《象》曰：澤上有雷，歸妹。君子以永終知敝。
image.en: The Image says: Above the lake there is thunder — the Marrying Maiden. The noble person thereby perpetuates what endures and understands what deteriorates.

1.zh: 初九，歸妹以娣，跛能履，征吉。
1.en: Initial Nine. The Marrying Maiden as a secondary bride. The lame can walk. To advance brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 少女而與長男為耦，非敵之謂，是娣從之義也。妹，少女之稱也。少女之行，善莫若娣。夫承嗣以君之子，雖幼而不妄行。少女以娣，雖跛能履，斯乃恒久之義，吉而相承之道也。以斯而進，吉其宜也。
wangBi.en: A youngest daughter paired with the eldest son — this is not what is meant by an equal match; it is the meaning of following as a secondary bride. 'Maiden' (mei) is a term for a younger sister. In the conduct of a younger sister, nothing is as good as serving as a secondary bride. Just as an heir who is the ruler's son, though young, does not act recklessly — so a younger sister serving as a secondary bride, though lame, can walk. This is the meaning of constancy and endurance, the Way of good fortune and mutual succession. To advance on this basis — good fortune is fitting.

2.zh: 《象》曰：利幽人之貞，未變常也。
2.en: The Image says: It is beneficial for a secluded person's Correctness — one has not departed from constancy.

wangBi.zh: 雖失其位，而居內處中，眇猶能視，足以保常也。在內履中，而能守其常，故利幽人之貞也。
wangBi.en: Although it has lost its proper position, it dwells within and occupies the center. The one-eyed can still see — this is sufficient to preserve constancy. Being within and treading in the center, and able to keep to constancy, hence it is beneficial for a secluded person's Correctness.

3.zh: 六三，歸妹以須，反歸以娣。
3.en: Six in the Third. The Marrying Maiden must wait. She returns and goes back as a secondary bride.

wangBi.zh: 室主猶存，而求進焉。進未值時，故有須也。不可以進，故反歸待時，以娣乃行也。
wangBi.en: The mistress of the household still remains, yet she seeks to advance. The advance does not meet the right time, hence there is waiting. She cannot advance, so she returns to wait for the right time, and only then goes forth as a secondary bride.

4.zh: 九四，歸妹愆期，遲歸有時。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth. The Marrying Maiden delays the date. The late marriage will come in its own time.

wangBi.zh: 夫以不正无應而適人也，必須彼道窮盡，无所與交，然後乃可以往，故愆期遲歸，以待時也。
wangBi.en: To go to another with an improper position and no corresponding line — one must wait until the other's way is exhausted and there is no one else to engage with, and only then can one go. Hence delaying the date and postponing the marriage, waiting for the right time.

5.zh: 六五，帝乙歸妹，其君之袂，不如其娣之袂良。月幾望，吉。
5.en: Six in the Fifth. Di Yi marries off his younger sister. The sovereign's sleeves are not as fine as those of her secondary bride. The moon is nearly full. Good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 歸妹之中，獨處貴位，故謂之帝乙歸妹也。袂，衣袖，所以為禮容者也。其君之袂，為帝乙所寵也，即五也。為帝乙所崇飾，故謂之其君之袂也。配在九二，兌少震長，以長從少，不若以少從長之為美也，故曰「不若其娣之袂良」也。位在乎中，以貴而行，極陰之盛，以斯適配，雖不若少，往亦必合，故曰「月幾望，吉」也。
wangBi.en: 'Sleeves' (mei) are the garment sleeves used for ceremonial deportment. 'The sovereign's sleeves' refers to the one favored by Di Yi, which is the fifth line. Being adorned and honored by Di Yi, hence it is called 'the sovereign's sleeves.' Her match is at Nine in the Second. Dui is the youngest and Zhen is the eldest; for the eldest to follow the youngest is not as fine as for the youngest to follow the eldest. Hence it says 'not as fine as those of her secondary bride.' Positioned in the center and proceeding with nobility, at the fullness of yin's flourishing — going to match with this, though not as fine as the younger, the union will surely be achieved. Hence it says 'the moon is nearly full — good fortune.'

6.zh: 上六，女承筐无實，士刲羊无血，无攸利。
6.en: Top Six. The woman holds a basket with nothing inside. The man slaughters the sheep but there is no blood. Nothing is of benefit.

wangBi.zh: 羊謂三也。處卦之窮，仰无所承，下又无應，為女而承命，則筐虛而莫之與。為士而下命，則刲羊而无血。刲羊而无血，不應所命也。進退莫與，故曰无攸利也。
wangBi.en: The sheep refers to the third line. Occupying the extremity of the hexagram, looking up there is nothing to receive from above, and below there is no corresponding line. As a woman receiving a command, the basket is empty and nothing is given to her. As a man issuing a command downward, one slaughters the sheep but there is no blood. Slaughtering the sheep with no blood means there is no response to the command. Advancing or retreating, nothing is given — hence it says 'nothing is of benefit.'

readouts.name: Abundance
readouts.question:
What will you
decide now?
readouts.lesson:
At your fullest,
light each corner.
readouts.finding: THUNDER AND FIRE AT ONCE: FULL.

image.zh: 《象》曰：雷電皆至，豐。君子以折獄致刑。
image.en: The Image says: Thunder and lightning both arrive—Abundance. The noble person thereby decides lawsuits and carries out punishments.

1.zh: 初九，遇其配主，雖旬无咎，往有尚。
1.en: Initial Nine. He meets his matching lord. Though they are equal, there is no blame. To go forth brings esteem.

wangBi.zh:
處豐之初，其配在四，以陽適陽，以明之動，能相光大者也。旬，均也。雖均无咎，往有尚也。初、四俱陽爻，故曰均也。

過均則爭，交斯叛也。
wangBi.en:
Dwelling at the beginning of Feng, its counterpart is in the fourth position. Yang going to yang, brilliance joined with movement—they are able to magnify and enlarge each other. Xun means 'equal.' Though equal, there is no blame; to go forth brings esteem. The first and fourth are both yang lines; hence they are called equal.

If equality is exceeded, there is contention; in their interaction, there would then be betrayal.

2.zh: 六二，豐其蔀，日中見斗。往得疑疾，有孚發若，吉。
2.en: Six in the Second. He makes abundant his screen of grass. At midday he sees the Dipper. Going forth, he encounters suspicion and hostility. With sincerity he arouses trust—auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 蔀，覆曖，鄣光明之物也。處明動之時，不能自豐以光大之德，既處乎內，而又以陰居陰，所豐在蔀，幽而无覩者也，故曰「豐其蔀，日中見斗」也。日中者，明之盛也。斗見者，闇之極也。處盛明而豐其蔀，故曰「日中見斗」。不能自發，故往得疑疾。然履中當位，處闇不邪，有孚者也。若，辭也。有孚可以發其志，不困於闇，故獲吉也。
wangBi.en: Bu is a covering that dims and obstructs light—a thing that blocks radiance. Dwelling in a time of brilliance and movement yet unable to make oneself abundant through the virtue of radiant greatness—already situated within the inner trigram, and moreover a yin line dwelling in a yin position—what is made abundant is the screen, dark with nothing visible. Hence it says 'he makes abundant his screen of grass; at midday he sees the Dipper.' Midday is the peak of brightness. The Dipper becoming visible is the extreme of darkness. Dwelling in peak brightness yet making abundant his screen; hence it says 'at midday he sees the Dipper.' Unable to bring himself forth, therefore going forth he encounters suspicion and hostility. Yet he treads the central position and occupies the proper place, dwelling in darkness without deviation—he possesses sincerity. Ruo is an expletive particle. With sincerity he can bring forth his resolve and is not trapped in darkness; therefore he obtains good fortune.

3.zh: 九三，豐其沛，日中見沬。折其右肱，无咎。
3.en: Nine in the Third. He makes abundant his curtain. At midday he sees tiny stars. He breaks his right arm—no blame.

wangBi.zh:
沛，幡幔，所以禦盛光也。沬，微昧之明也。應在上六，志在乎陰，雖愈乎以陰處陰，亦未足以免於闇也。所豐在沛，日中見沬之謂也。施明則見沬而已，施用則折其右肱，故可以自守而已，未足用也。

明不足也。

雖有左在，不足用也。
wangBi.en:
Pei is a pennant curtain, used to ward off bright light. Mei is a faint, dim illumination. Its correspondence is with Top Six; its inclination is toward yin. Though better than a yin line dwelling in a yin position, it is still insufficient to escape darkness. What is made abundant is the curtain; this is what 'at midday he sees tiny stars' means. In applying brilliance, one merely sees tiny stars; in applying function, one breaks one's right arm. Therefore one can only maintain self-preservation; it is insufficient for use.

Brilliance is insufficient.

Though the left arm remains, it is insufficient for use.

4.zh: 九四，豐其蔀，日中見斗。遇其夷主，吉。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth. He makes abundant his screen of grass. At midday he sees the Dipper. He meets his equal lord—auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 以陽居陰，豐其蔀也。得初以發，夷主吉也。
wangBi.en: A yang line dwelling in a yin position—this is making abundant his screen of grass. Obtaining the first line to bring forth brilliance—the equal lord brings good fortune.

5.zh: 六五，來章有慶譽，吉。
5.en: Six in the Fifth. Brilliance comes; there will be celebration and praise—auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 以陰之質，來適尊陽之位，能自光大，章顯其德，獲慶譽也。
wangBi.en: With the substance of yin, it comes to take up the honored yang position. Able to make itself radiant and great, it makes its virtue luminous and manifest, thereby obtaining celebration and praise.

6.zh: 上六，豐其屋，蔀其家，闚其戶，闃其无人。三歲不覿，凶。
6.en: Top Six. He makes abundant his roof, screens his household. Peering through his door—silent, with no one there. For three years he is not seen—misfortune.

wangBi.zh:
屋，藏蔭之物，以陰處極而最在外，不履於位，深自幽隱，絕跡深藏者也。既豐其屋，又蔀其家，屋厚家覆，闇之甚也。雖闚其戶，闃其无人，棄其所處，而自深藏也。處於明動尚大之時而深自幽隱，以高其行；大道既濟，而猶不見，隱不為賢，更為反道，凶其宜也。三年，豐道之成。治道未濟，隱猶可也；既濟而隱，以治為亂也。

翳光最甚者也。

可以出而不出，自藏之謂也，非有為而藏。不出戶庭，失時致凶，況自藏乎？凶其宜也。
wangBi.en:
Wu (roof/house) is a thing that shelters and shades. A yin line dwelling at the extreme and furthest outside, not treading upon a proper position—one who deeply hides oneself in seclusion, cutting off all traces and concealing oneself in the depths. Having made abundant his roof and further screened his household—the roof thick and the household covered—the darkness is extreme. Though one peers through his door, it is silent with no one there; he has abandoned his proper place and hidden himself in the depths. Dwelling in a time of brilliance, movement, and esteem for greatness, yet deeply hiding in seclusion to elevate his conduct—when the great Way has already been accomplished yet he still does not appear, hiding does not constitute worthiness but rather goes against the Way. Misfortune is fitting for him. Three years is the completion of the Way of Feng. When the Way of governance has not yet been accomplished, hiding is still acceptable; once accomplished yet still hiding, one treats good order as disorder.

This is the most extreme eclipse of light.

Able to come forth yet not coming forth—this is what is meant by hiding oneself; it is not hiding for a purposeful reason. If merely not going out through the door and courtyard causes one to miss the moment and bring about misfortune, how much more so when one actively hides oneself! Misfortune is fitting indeed.

readouts.name: The Gentle
meaning:
The Gentle says:
say it again.
readouts.question:
What’s worth
repeating today?
readouts.lesson:
Bend only to
what is right.
readouts.finding: EACH SOFT LINE SITS UNDER A STRONG.

image.zh: 《象》曰：隨風，巽，君子以申命行事。
image.en: The Image states: Following winds—Xun. The noble person uses this to reiterate commands and carry out affairs.

1.en: Initial Six: Advancing and retreating. Benefit in the correctness of a military person.

wangBi.zh:
處令之初，未能服令者也。故進退也。成命齊邪，莫善武人，故利武人之貞以整之。

巽順之志，進退疑懼。
wangBi.en:
Situated at the beginning of the command, this is one who cannot yet submit to the command, hence the advancing and retreating. To enforce commands and bring the deviant into line, nothing is better than a military person—hence the benefit in a military person's correctness to bring order.

With a disposition of compliant submission, one advances and retreats in doubt and apprehension.

2.zh: 九二，巽在牀下，用史巫紛若，吉，无咎。
2.en: Nine in the Second: Compliant beneath the bed. Employing scribes and shamans in profusion—auspicious, no blame.

wangBi.zh: 處巽之中，既在下位，而復以陽居陰，卑巽之甚，故曰「巽在牀下」也。卑甚失正，則入于咎過矣。能以居中而施至卑於神祗，而不用之於威勢，則乃至于紛若之吉，而亡其過矣。故曰「用史巫紛若，吉，无咎」也。
wangBi.en: Situated at the center of the Xun trigram, already in a lower position, and further having a yang line occupying a yin position—the humility and compliance are extreme. Hence it says 'compliant beneath the bed.' When humility is extreme and correctness is lost, one falls into blame and error. If one can, by virtue of occupying the central position, direct this utmost humility toward the spirits and deities rather than employing it toward those with power and authority, then one attains the auspiciousness of profusion and eliminates one's errors. Hence it says 'employing scribes and shamans in profusion—auspicious, no blame.'

3.zh: 九三，頻巽，吝。
3.en: Nine in the Third: Repeatedly compliant with a furrowed brow—humiliation.

wangBi.zh: 頻，頻蹙，不樂而窮，不得已之謂也。以其剛正而為四所乘，志窮而巽，是以吝也。
wangBi.en: 'Pin' (頻) means furrowed and frowning—unhappy and exhausted, referring to what is done out of compulsion. Being firm and correct yet ridden upon by the fourth line, its intent is exhausted and yet it must comply. This is why there is humiliation.

4.zh: 六四，悔亡，田獲三品。
4.en: Six in the Fourth: Regret vanishes. In the hunt, three kinds of game are caught.

wangBi.zh: 乘剛，悔也，然得位承五，卑得所奉。雖以柔御剛，而依尊履正，以斯行命，必能獲強暴，遠不仁者也。獲而有益，莫善三品，故曰「悔亡，田獲三品」。一曰乾豆，二曰賓客，三曰充君之包。
wangBi.en: Riding upon the firm is cause for regret. However, it obtains its proper position and serves the fifth line; in its humility it finds one to serve. Although the yielding controls the firm, it relies on the honored one and treads on correctness. Using this to carry out commands, it will surely be able to capture the violent and keep the inhumane at a distance. For catching game that is beneficial, nothing surpasses the three categories—hence it says 'regret vanishes; in the hunt, three kinds of game are caught.' The first is for the dried sacrificial vessels, the second is for guests and visitors, the third is to stock the ruler's kitchen.

5.zh: 九五，貞吉，悔亡，无不利。无初有終。先庚三日，後庚三日，吉。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth: Correctness brings auspiciousness, regret vanishes, nothing is unfavorable. No beginning, but there is an end. Three days before geng, three days after geng—auspicious.

wangBi.zh: 以陽居陽，損於謙巽。然秉乎中正以宣其令，物莫之違，故曰「貞吉，悔亡，无不利」也。化不以漸，卒以剛直用加於物，故初皆不說也。終於中正，邪道以消，故有終也。申命令謂之庚。夫以正齊物，不可卒也；民迷固久，直不可肆也，故先申三日，令著之後，復申三日，然後誅而无咎怨矣。甲、庚，皆申命之謂也。
wangBi.en: Having a yang line occupy a yang position diminishes humble compliance. Yet by holding to centrality and correctness to proclaim commands, nothing disobeys—hence it says 'correctness brings auspiciousness, regret vanishes, nothing is unfavorable.' When transformation does not proceed gradually and one abruptly applies firmness and directness to things, at first none are pleased—hence 'no beginning.' In the end, through centrality and correctness, deviant ways are eliminated—hence 'there is an end.' The reiteration of commands is called 'geng.' Now, to align things through correctness cannot be done abruptly; the people's confusion has solidified over a long time, and directness cannot be given free rein. Therefore one first reiterates for three days, and after the command has been made clear, one reiterates again for three days. Only then does one punish, and there will be no blame or resentment. Both 'jia' and 'geng' refer to the reiteration of commands.

6.zh: 上九，巽在牀下，喪其資斧，貞凶。
6.en: Top Nine: Compliant beneath the bed. Loses the resources and the axe. Correctness brings misfortune.

wangBi.zh: 處巽之極，極巽過甚，故曰「巽在牀下」也。斧所以斷者也，過巽失正，喪所以斷，故曰「喪其資斧，貞凶」也。
wangBi.en: Situated at the extreme of Xun, the compliance is excessive and goes too far—hence it says 'compliant beneath the bed.' The axe is that by which one cuts decisively. Excessive compliance loses correctness, and one loses the means to cut decisively—hence it says 'loses the resources and the axe; correctness brings misfortune.'

readouts.name: Dispersion
meaning:
Remind them where
they come from.
readouts.question:
What do you
all share?
readouts.lesson:
Bring them back
to the centre.
readouts.finding: WIND MOVES OVER WATER.

image.zh: 《象》曰：風行水上，渙，先王以享于帝，立廟。
image.en: The Image says: Wind moves over the water—Dispersion. The former kings accordingly made offerings to the Supreme Deity and established ancestral temples.

1.en: Initial Six. Using rescue, the horse is strong. Auspicious.

wangBi.zh:
渙，散也。處散之初，乖散未甚，故可以遊行，得其志而違於難也，不在危劇而後乃逃竄，故曰「用拯馬壯，吉」。

觀難而行，不與險爭，故曰順也。
wangBi.en:
Huan means to scatter. Being at the beginning of scattering, the divergence and dispersal are not yet severe; hence one can travel freely, attaining one's purpose while avoiding difficulty. One does not wait until the danger is extreme before fleeing; hence it says 'using rescue, the horse is strong—auspicious.'

Observing the difficulty and then acting, not contending with danger—hence it says 'compliance.'

2.zh: 九二，渙奔其机，悔亡。
2.en: Nine in the Second. In Dispersion, one rushes to the bench. Regret vanishes.

wangBi.zh: 机，承物者也，謂初也。二俱无應，與初相得，而初得散道，離散而奔，得其所安，故悔亡也。
wangBi.en: Ji (bench) is that which supports things—it refers to the first line. The second line has no corresponding line, and is paired with the first. The first obtains the Way of Dispersion; scattering and rushing, it finds its place of rest. Hence regret vanishes.

3.zh: 六三，渙其躬，无悔。
3.en: Six in the Third. Dispersing one's own self. No regret.

wangBi.zh: 渙之為義，內險而外安者也。散躬志外，不固所守，與剛合志，故得无悔也。
wangBi.en: The meaning of Dispersion is that the inside is dangerous while the outside is secure. Dispersing one's own self with one's purpose directed outward, not clinging stubbornly to what one holds, and sharing purpose with the firm—hence one attains no regret.

4.zh: 六四，渙其群，元吉。渙，有丘匪夷，所思。
4.en: Six in the Fourth. Dispersing the group—Sublime Beginning auspiciousness. In Dispersion, there are hills that are not level—something to ponder.

wangBi.zh: 踰乎險難，得位體巽，與五合志，內掌機密，外宣化命者也，故能散群之險，以光其道。然處於卑順，不可自專，而為散之任，猶有丘虛匪夷之慮，雖得元吉，所思不可忘也。
wangBi.en: Having crossed beyond danger and difficulty, obtaining its position and embodying Xun (compliance), sharing its purpose with the fifth line, inwardly managing confidential affairs and outwardly proclaiming transformative commands—hence it is able to disperse the group's dangers and thereby make its Way shine. However, being in a lowly and compliant position, it cannot act on its own authority. In carrying out the charge of Dispersion, there are still concerns about hills and mounds that are not level. Although one obtains Sublime Beginning auspiciousness, what must be pondered should not be forgotten.

5.zh: 九五，渙汗其大號，渙，王居无咎。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth. In Dispersion, one sweats forth the great proclamation. In Dispersion, the king dwells here—no blame.

wangBi.zh:
處尊履正，居巽之中，散汗大號，以蕩險阨者也。為渙之主，唯王居之，乃得无咎也。

正位不可以假人。
wangBi.en:
Occupying the honored position and treading upon correctness, dwelling in the center of Xun (compliance), sweating forth the great proclamation to sweep away dangers and hardships. As the master of Dispersion, only the king may dwell in this position, and only then is there no blame.

The correct position cannot be lent to another.

6.zh: 上九，渙其血，去逖出，无咎。
6.en: Top Nine. Dispersing the blood. Departing, going far away and out. No blame.

wangBi.zh: 逖，遠也。最遠於害，不近侵克，散其憂傷，遠出者也。散患於遠害之地，誰將咎之哉！
wangBi.en: Ti means distant. Being farthest from harm and not close to aggression and attack, one disperses one's grief and sorrow and goes far away. Dispersing troubles in a place far from harm—who would assign blame!

readouts.name: Limitation
readouts.question:
Where’s your
limit?
readouts.lesson:
A lake holds only
so much water.
readouts.finding: THE STRONG HOLDS THE CENTRE.

image.zh: 《象》曰：澤上有水，節。君子以制數度，議德行。
image.en: The Image says: Above the lake there is water—Regulation. The noble person thereby establishes numerical measures and deliberates upon virtue and conduct.

1.en: Initial Nine. Not going out through the door of the courtyard. No blame.

wangBi.zh: 為節之初，將整離散而立制度者也，故明於通塞，慮於險偽，不出戶庭，慎密不失，然後事濟而无咎也。
wangBi.en: Being at the beginning of Regulation, this is one who will bring order to what has been scattered and establish institutional measures. Therefore one discerns clearly between what is open and what is blocked, considers carefully the dangers of deception, does not go out through the door of the courtyard, and maintains cautious secrecy without lapse. Only then are affairs brought to completion without blame.

2.zh: 九二，不出門庭，凶。
2.en: Nine in the Second. Not going out through the gate of the courtyard. Misfortune.

wangBi.zh: 初已造之，至二宜宣其制矣，而故匿之，失時之極，則遂廢矣。故不出門庭，則凶也。
wangBi.en: The first line has already created the regulations; by the time one reaches the second, it is fitting to promulgate those measures. Yet one deliberately conceals them, missing the critical moment to the utmost degree, and consequently they fall into neglect. Therefore, not going out through the gate of the courtyard leads to misfortune.

3.zh: 六三，不節若，則嗟若，无咎。
3.en: Six in the Third. If one does not regulate, then one will lament. No blame.

wangBi.zh: 若，辭也。以陰處陽，以柔乘剛，違節之道，以至哀嗟。自己所致，无所怨咎，故曰无咎也。
wangBi.en: Ruo is a particle. Occupying a yang position with a yin line, and a yielding line riding atop a firm line, one violates the Way of regulation to the point of mournful lamentation. This is brought about by oneself; there is no one else to blame. Hence it says 'no blame.'

4.zh: 六四，安節，亨。
4.en: Six in the Fourth. Peaceful regulation. Success.

wangBi.zh: 得位而順，不改其節，而能亨者也。承上以斯，得其道也。
wangBi.en: Having attained the proper position and being compliant, one does not alter one's regulation and is thereby able to achieve success. Serving the one above in this manner, one attains the Way.

5.zh: 九五，甘節，吉。往有尚。
5.en: Nine in the Fifth. Sweet regulation. Auspicious. Going forth, there is esteem.

wangBi.zh: 當位居中，為節之主不失其中，不傷財，不害民之謂也。為節而不苦，非甘而何？術斯以往，往有尚也。
wangBi.en: Occupying the proper position and dwelling in the center, as the master of regulation one does not lose the mean. This is what is meant by 'not wasting resources and not harming the people.' To regulate without bitterness—if not sweet, then what? Proceeding forth by this method, going forth there is esteem.

6.zh: 上六，苦節，貞凶，悔亡。
6.en: Top Six. Bitter regulation. Correctness brings misfortune. Regret vanishes.

wangBi.zh: 過節之中，以致亢極，苦節者也。以斯施人*，物所不堪，正之凶也。以斯脩身，行在无妄，故得悔亡。
wangBi.en: Exceeding the center of regulation to the point of reaching the utmost extreme—this is bitter regulation. If one applies this to governing others*, things cannot endure it; this is the misfortune of correctness. If one applies this to cultivating oneself, one's conduct is free from recklessness, and therefore regret vanishes.

readouts.name: Before Completion
meaning:
Sort things out
before you move.
readouts.question:
What goes
where?
readouts.lesson:
Almost across,
the fox gets wet.
readouts.finding:
LINES 2–5 OUT OF POSITION.
ALL THREE PAIRS ANSWER.

image.zh: 《象》曰：火在水上，未濟，君子以慎辨物居方。
image.en: The Image says: Fire above water—Not Yet Across. The noble person thereby carefully distinguishes things and assigns them to their proper places.

1.en: Initial Six. Wets its tail. Regret.

wangBi.zh: 處未濟之初，最居險下，不可以濟者也。而欲之其應，進則溺身。未濟之始，始於既濟之上六也。濡其首猶不反，至于濡其尾，不知紀極者也。然以陰處下，非為進亢，遂其志者也。困則能反，故不曰凶。事在己量，而必困乃反，頑亦甚矣，故曰吝也。
wangBi.en: Situated at the beginning of Not Yet Across, dwelling at the very bottom of danger—one who cannot cross. Yet wishing to go to its correspondent, advancing would drown the self. The beginning of Not Yet Across begins from the Top Six of Already Across. If wetting the head still does not make one turn back, and it reaches the point of wetting the tail, this shows one who does not know where to stop. However, being yin dwelling below, it is not one that presses forward aggressively to fulfill its ambition. When in difficulty, it is able to turn back, and therefore the text does not say 'misfortune.' The matter lies in one's own judgment, yet one must be in difficulty before turning back—this is exceedingly obstinate. Hence it says 'regret.'

2.zh: 九二，曳其輪，貞吉。
2.en: Nine in the Second. Dragging back the wheels. Correctness brings good fortune.

wangBi.zh:
體剛履中，而應於五，五體陰柔，應與而不自任者也。居未濟之時，處險難之中，體剛中之質，而見任與，拯救危難，經綸屯蹇者也。用健拯難*，靖難*在正，而不違中，故「曳其輪，貞吉」也。

位雖不正，中以行正也。
wangBi.en:
Its substance is firm and it treads the center, corresponding with the fifth. The fifth is yin and yielding in substance, corresponding with and relying upon it rather than taking charge itself. Dwelling in the time of Not Yet Across, situated in the midst of danger, with the quality of firm centrality, it is entrusted and relied upon to rescue from peril and manage difficulties amid distress and obstruction. Employing strength to rescue from difficulty*, bringing peace to difficulty* through correctness, and not deviating from the center—hence 'dragging back the wheels, correctness brings good fortune.'

Although the position is not proper, through centrality one acts with correctness.

3.zh: 六三，未濟，征凶，利涉大川。
3.en: Six in the Third. Not yet across. To advance brings misfortune. It is beneficial to cross the great river.

wangBi.zh: 以陰之質，失位居險，不能自濟者也。以不正之身，力不能自濟，而求進焉，喪其身也。故曰征凶也。二能拯難，而己比之，棄己委二，載二而行，溺可得乎？何憂未濟，故曰利涉大川。
wangBi.en: With the quality of yin, it has lost its proper position and dwells in danger—one who cannot save itself. With an improper position, its strength is insufficient to save itself; if it seeks to advance, it will lose its life. Hence it says 'to advance brings misfortune.' The second is able to rescue from difficulty, and this line is close beside it. If one abandons self-reliance and entrusts oneself to the second, being carried by the second and proceeding, can drowning then occur? Why worry about Not Yet Across? Hence it says 'it is beneficial to cross the great river.'

4.zh: 九四，貞吉，悔亡。震用伐鬼方，三年有賞于大國。
4.en: Nine in the Fourth. Correctness brings good fortune. Regret vanishes. With a thunderous campaign one attacks the Gui Fang. After three years, there is reward from a great state.

wangBi.zh: 處未濟之時，而出險難之上，居文明之初，體乎剛質，以近至尊。雖履非其位，志在乎正，則吉而悔亡矣。其志得行，靡禁其威，故曰「震用伐鬼方」也。「伐鬼方」者，興衰之征也。故每至興衰而取義焉。處文明之初，始出於難，其德未盛，故曰三年也。五居尊以柔，體乎文明之盛，不奪物功者也，故以大國賞之也。
wangBi.en: Situated in the time of Not Yet Across, having emerged above the danger, dwelling at the beginning of cultural brilliance, with a firm quality of substance, and close to the supreme ruler. Although it treads a position that is not its own, its resolve is set upon correctness, and thus it is fortunate and regret vanishes. Its resolve is carried out and nothing restrains its awesome power, hence it says 'with a thunderous campaign one attacks the Gui Fang.' 'Attacking the Gui Fang' is a sign of rise and decline; hence whenever rise and decline occur, this meaning is invoked. Dwelling at the beginning of cultural brilliance, having just emerged from difficulty, its virtue is not yet abundant, hence it says 'three years.' The fifth dwells in the honored position with yielding, embodying the fullness of cultural brilliance, and does not usurp the merit of others. Therefore it rewards with a great state.

5.zh: 六五，貞吉，无悔。君子之光，有孚，吉。
5.en: Six in the Fifth. Correctness brings good fortune. No regret. The light of the noble person. There is sincerity. Good fortune.

wangBi.zh: 以柔居尊，處文明之盛，為未濟之主，故必正然後乃吉，吉乃得无悔也。夫以柔順文明之質，居於尊位，付與於能，而不自役，使武以文，御剛以柔，斯誠君子之光也。付物以能，而不疑也，物則竭力，功斯克矣，故曰「有孚，吉。」
wangBi.en: Dwelling in the honored position with yielding, situated at the fullness of cultural brilliance, serving as the ruler of Not Yet Across—therefore one must be correct and only then is there good fortune; with good fortune one then attains no regret. Now, with the quality of yielding compliance and cultural brilliance, dwelling in the honored position, delegating to the capable without laboring oneself, directing the martial through the civil and governing the firm through the yielding—this is truly the light of the noble person. Entrusting others with tasks according to their abilities without doubting them, others then exert their utmost strength, and merit is thereby achieved. Hence it says 'there is sincerity, good fortune.'

6.zh: 上九，有孚于飲酒，无咎。濡其首，有孚失是。
6.en: Top Nine. There is sincerity in drinking wine. No blame. Wets its head. Having sincerity, one loses what is right.

wangBi.zh: 未濟之極，則反於既濟。既濟之道，所任者當也。所任者當，則可信之无疑，而己逸焉，故曰「有孚於飲酒，无咎」也。以其能信於物，故得逸豫而不憂於事之廢。苟不憂於事之廢，而耽於樂之甚，則至於失節矣。由於有孚，失於是矣，故曰「濡其首，有孚，失是」也。
wangBi.en: At the extreme of Not Yet Across, it reverts to Already Across. The Way of Already Across is that those entrusted with responsibilities are fitting. When those entrusted are fitting, one can trust them without doubt and enjoy leisure oneself. Hence it says 'there is sincerity in drinking wine, no blame.' Because one is able to trust others, one attains ease and comfort without worrying that affairs will be neglected. But if one does not worry about affairs being neglected and indulges excessively in pleasure, then one reaches the point of losing restraint. It is through having sincerity that one loses what is right. Hence it says 'wets its head; having sincerity, one loses what is right.'
